successors.note: 'Under Augustus the territory was incorporated into Gallia Belgica', under the Flavians into Germania Superior (no years on the page); the eastern part went to the Rauraci, 'who gained independence after his defeat'.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Sequani row. The page has no infobox and gives no area ('town sizes only'); the four Franche-Comte departments come to about 16,700 km2 and with Haut-Rhin to about 20,000 km2 by the gazetteer. The eastern extension is the researcher's reading of 'the eastern part of their lands'.

keyframe_review.note: After the Germanic settlement 'around 70 BC' the eastern part of the lands was lost to Ariovistus (the Sequani page; the Ariovistus page puts his settlers in Alsace). The Franche-Comte core stays: Caesar wintered two legions 'in Sequanian territory' in 58 and the Sequani sent 12,000 men to the Gallic coalition in 52.

ledger.note: The Sequani hold the Saône-Doubs country round Vesontio and the Jura passes. The page gives no founding date ('long at odds with the Aedui'); 100 is a placeholder (page silent).

ledger.note: c. 70 BC: Germanic settlers take the east. 'Germanic groups occupied part of Sequanian territory around 70 BC'; 'The Germanic king Ariovistus, whom the Sequani had called in, settled on the left bank of the Rhine and turned against his former allies'. The Ariovistus page says he took a third of the territory of the Aedui, not the Sequani, at Magetobriga (61): the pages disagree.

ledger.note: September 52 BC: the Sequani, who had sent 12,000 men to the coalition, fall under Rome with Alesia, which 'proved to be the end of generalized and organized resistance'. Neither page dates the Sequani's submission; this is the researcher's bridge to the Roman annexation under Augustus.

wars.name: Gallic Wars: Battle of the Vosges against Ariovistus (58 BC)
wars.outcome: Caesar, at the Aedui's request, defeated the coalition of Ariovistus, who 'escaped across the Rhine'; the Sequani's ascendancy 'among the peoples of eastern Gaul' was broken and Labienus's two legions wintered in their territory.
wars.note: Ariovistus page: 'driven back over the Rhine in 58 BC'; the site is uncertain (Belfort region, Mulhouse-Basel plain, Ribeauville, Cernay).

certainty.note: The Jura and the Saone are the limits the page gives; the Rhine side is undefined.

notes: New state, not in Cliopatria. Thin: no infobox, no area, no start. Pages disagree on whose third of land Ariovistus seized: the Sequani page says the Sequani's, the Ariovistus page says the Aedui's (at Magetobriga, 61), turning on the Sequani only later; neither is drawn beyond the c. 70 BC loss of the east. The Sequani page dates Magetobriga 61-60, the Ariovistus page 61. The 52 end is a bridge (confidence 1): the Sequani page says only that they sent a 12,000-man contingent; an Ariovistus dossier (Germanic settlers in Alsace, c. 71-58) and a Rauraci one may be wanted. Wikidata id left null. Family 'france' is a registry key.
